blocks.text: Banking exams love to check whether you know the plain-English meaning of everyday money words. This section covers what happens inside a bank account, how people earn and spend, and the compulsory payments they make.

blocks.title: Working with an account
rows: The money sitting in a savings or current account. It can also mean the amount still left to be repaid on a loan.
Taking money out of an account.
Trying to take out more than the balance available in the account.
Situation where a cheque is written for more than the account holds. The bank may return the cheque and usually levies a penalty fee.
Fees a financial institution levies on account holders for the upkeep and maintenance of their accounts.
An account in which the investor earns interest on the balance but must maintain a minimum balance.
A fixed amount deposited for a fixed term to earn interest. Withdrawing early attracts a penalty.

blocks.title: Income, spending and tax
rows: A written or electronic plan for managing your finances and saving money.
Money received as wages for work done.
Money made without working for it, for example interest earned on savings.
Money spent on needs and wants.
Payments that stay the same every month, such as a car instalment.
Payments that change from month to month, such as groceries or utility bills.
Compulsory fees a government charges its citizens to run the government.

blocks.title: Earned or unearned?
blocks.text: Salary, wages and a freelancer's fees are earned income because you worked for them. Interest on a deposit is unearned income. A withdrawal is just your own money coming back, not income at all.

blocks.title: Borrowing basics
rows: Money borrowed that the borrower must repay.
Money or goods owed to another person or entity.
A legal contract in which a lender gives money for the borrower to use. The borrower normally pays interest and must repay within a fixed time.
The amount borrowed, without interest. For an investor it is the amount invested.
The fee lenders charge, as a percentage of the loan amount, for lending the money.
Interest plus fees charged on a loan over one year, expressed as a percentage.
The equally divided monthly payment that clears an outstanding loan within the agreed time.
Paying off a debt through a fixed schedule of equal payments of principal and interest until the end of the loan term.
The smallest amount a loan or card account requires each period. Borrowers may always pay more.
A percentage of the loan amount that a lender may add, payable as a one-time lump sum.

blocks.title: Credit cards and credit history
rows: A purchase made on a revolving credit account. Interest applies unless the full amount is paid before the grace period ends.
Fee a lender charges for lending money. Paying the balance within the grace period avoids it.
On revolving credit cards, the window in which paying the full balance means no interest or finance charges.
The record of borrowing and repaying that a person builds. Lenders check it before giving future loans.
Card for building credit: the customer first deposits money, then makes charges only up to that balance.

blocks.title: How a loan runs from start to trouble
items: Principal, rate and term are fixed
Last resort when debt is hopeless

blocks.title: Security, default and recovery
rows: Property pledged to assure repayment of a loan.
An additional party added to a loan contract who guarantees payment if the borrower defaults.
A lender's legal right over a property in connection with a debt, which it can enforce if the borrower defaults.
The loan taken to buy real estate.
Failing to make a payment as the agreement requires.
Legal proceedings in which the lender seizes the property behind a secured debt. A mortgage default can end in foreclosure and auction.
Legal protection from debts for a person or company that cannot repay them. It can involve selling assets to reduce the debt.
An in-depth examination of a person's or company's finances by an auditor.

blocks.title: Interest vs rate vs APR
blocks.text: Interest is the money fee. Interest rate is the percentage. APR goes further and includes fees too, measured over one year. A lien is the right over property, and foreclosure is the act of actually seizing it.

blocks.title: Assets and investments
rows: Something you own, such as property, money, or investments like stocks and bonds.
Using money to buy things or placing it in particular accounts in order to earn a profit.
An asset or investment rises in value.
An asset losing value over time through wear and tear.
A series of equal payments made at regular intervals. Annuities include compound interest.
Debt instrument issued by a government or corporation. The issuer pays interest and the face value at the end of the term.
Tangible goods such as gold or wheat in which people invest hoping prices will rise.
Paper or electronic instruments that prove ownership of stocks or bonds.

blocks.title: Ownership and returns
rows: Issued by a company to certify that an investor owns part of it.
One unit of ownership in a company.
A company's payment to its stockholders to share profit.
A pool of investors holding a collection of different assets together, which gives diversification.
Spreading investment money across different kinds of investments to reduce risk.
What an investor gains after subtracting the principal and any extra costs from the final amount.
The money coming back to an account holder from an investment.
The likelihood that the investor will lose money on the deal.
The single person who owns a business.

blocks.title: Stock vs share vs bond
blocks.text: Stock and shares mean ownership, and dividends flow from profits. A bond means you are a lender, so you get interest and the face value back. Two different relationships with the issuer.
From here the chapter becomes a look-up list of abbreviations. Learn them in groups, the way they are used in real life. This first group covers how money and messages move between banks.

blocks.title: Payment systems and channels
rows: Funds settled one transaction at a time, in real time
Dues netted off and settled later, not one by one
Largest network of shared ATMs in India
Cash from ATMs without a card; RBI announced it on 8 April 2022
Central unit of the bill payment system
Charge on merchants for accepting card payments
RBI app that helps identify currency notes
Code identifying a bank branch for electronic transfers

blocks.title: Messaging and cheque clearing
rows: Network of the Indian banking sector
Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunications
Cheque image moves instead of the paper cheque
The I is Interface; used in CTS
Ensures security, integrity and authenticity of CTS data and images

blocks.title: SFMS or SWIFT?
blocks.text: SFMS has the word Structured and works inside India over INFINET, the Indian network. SWIFT has Worldwide in its name, so it is the international one.

blocks.title: Rates, loans and ratios
rows: Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate

blocks.title: BPLR and MCLR
blocks.phrase: Both end in Lending Rate. B comes before M in the alphabet, and BPLR (Benchmark) was the older system, MCLR (Marginal Cost) the newer one.
letters: Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate
Annual Percentage Rate (cost of a loan per year)
blocks.note: Exam trap: the L in MCLR and BPLR is Lending, never Leading or Large.

blocks.title: Institutions, deposits and balance sheet
rows: Net Satisfaction Factor in the source list; on cheques it usually means Non-Sufficient Funds

blocks.title: NSF and FRB have two readings
blocks.text: In the source list NSF is given as Net Satisfaction Factor, but on a bounced cheque it stands for non-sufficient funds. Likewise FRB means Federal Reserve Board in the list, while an insurance question uses it for Foreign Reinsurance Branches. Read the context.

blocks.title: Exchanges, depositories and instruments
rows: Securities Exchange Commission (as written in the source list)
Association of Mutual Funds in India

blocks.title: ROA, ROE, ROI
blocks.phrase: A-E-I, the vowels in order: ROA for Assets, ROE for Equity, ROI for Investment.
blocks.note: Only the last letter changes, so tie A, E, I to Assets, Equity, Investment.

blocks.title: Fiscal, tax and schemes
rows: Accelerated Power Development and Reform Programme

blocks.title: Big-picture economy words
blocks.text: GDP is the total market value of all final goods and services produced in a country in a year. GNP adds income earned by citizens abroad and leaves out foreigners' income at home. The PMI measures business activity in both manufacturing and services.

blocks.title: The W-family
blocks.phrase: Two Wholesale, two Working, one Ways, one Wholly, one Weighted: WPI and WDM, WC and WCDL, WMA, WOS, WADR.
blocks.note: Odd-one-out questions often mix these: WPI measures prices, WDM is a market, WMA is an RBI advance to the government.

blocks.title: Date-to-date order
blocks.text: MTD, QTD and YTD get longer in the order Month, Quarter, Year. MTD covers the least time and YTD the most.
These abbreviations and terms have come up repeatedly in bank exam papers. Many are tricky because the wrong options look almost right, so learn the exact wording.

blocks.title: Past-paper full forms
rows: Business activity in manufacturing and services
RBI changes rates and ratios under it
The M is Monopolies; the Act no longer applies
A form for filing an income tax return
Recommends suitable products from the whole market
Framework to judge sustainability and ethical practice
Insurers whose failure would hurt the financial system
Unique 20-character global code for a legal entity
Helps the public find unclaimed deposits across banks
Food processing scheme of the Ministry of Food Processing Industries
A financial company that is not a bank

blocks.title: Look-alike options
blocks.text: Exams change one word: Managers or Management (PMI), Lending or Leading (MCLR), Minimum or Maximum (MSP), Equated or Equal (EMI), Interoperable or Integrated (ICCW). Always read the whole phrase.

blocks.title: Dates from the past-year questions
items: Public Provident Fund (PPF) introduced by the National Savings Institute of the Ministry of Finance.
SEBI set up as a statutory body; the SEBI Act came into force on 30 January 1992.
First Exchange Traded Fund in India launched by Nippon India Mutual Fund (formerly Benchmark) on the Nifty 50 Index.
RBI advised banks to offer Basic Savings Bank Deposit (no-frills) accounts to promote financial inclusion.
RBI announced the Interoperable Cardless Cash Withdrawal facility.

blocks.title: Facts behind the abbreviations
rows: Interest was 7.1 percent a year, set by the Ministry of Finance each year, compounded annually and paid on 31 March. The account matures after 15 years, and partial withdrawal is allowed after 6 years in special circumstances.
Transfers benefits straight into Aadhaar-linked bank accounts of beneficiaries under 34 central schemes. It removes diversion and duplicate payments.
Normal banking service for all with no minimum balance requirement (zero balance account).
Covered under FEMA 1999. Exports and imports can be invoiced and paid in rupees, with the exchange rate market determined.
Notes that have become dirty and slightly cut. Rs 10 and higher notes in two pieces also count as soiled if the cut did not pass through the number panels.
Minimum capital requirement cut from Rs 100 crore to Rs 50 crore (as per the 2023 exam question).
LIC, GIC and New India Assurance named as Domestic Systemically Important Insurers by the insurance regulator. They face higher supervision.
Unique 20-character global identifier. SEBI introduced it for entities planning to list non-convertible securities, securitised debt instruments and security receipts.
The value of the IMF's Special Drawing Right is set by a basket of 5 currencies: US Dollar, Japanese Yen, British Pound, Chinese Yuan and Euro.

blocks.title: Five currencies in the SDR basket
blocks.note: Five words, five currencies. If the question asks how many, the answer is 5.

blocks.title: Years and numbers
blocks.phrase: SEBI '92 and ETF '02 both end in 2. PPF: 15 to mature, 6 to peek. LEI is 20 characters, FRB capital halves from 100 to 50 crore.
letters: 1968; matures after 15 years; partial withdrawal after 6 years
Capital Rs 100 crore to Rs 50 crore
blocks.note: DBT started on New Year's Day 2013, so remember 1-1-2013.

revision: Unearned income is money made from interest; earned income is wages for work done.
Collateral is pledged property; a cosigner guarantees payment; a lien gives the lender a legal right over the property.
A default on a mortgage can lead to foreclosure, where the lender seizes and auctions the property.
APR is interest plus fees over one year; EMI is an Equated Monthly Installment.
A bond makes you a lender, while a stock or share makes you an owner.
BPLR is Benchmark Prime Lending Rate and MCLR is Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate.
RTGS is Real Time Gross Settlement; SFMS runs on INFINET inside India, SWIFT works internationally.
CHI (Clearing House Interface), PKI (Public Key Infrastructure) and CCP (Cheque Collection Policy) belong to cheque clearing.
NFS is the National Financial Switch, the largest network of shared ATMs in India.
ROA, ROE and ROI are Return on Assets, Equity and Investment (A, E, I in order).
FRBM is Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management; GFD is Gross Fiscal Deficit.
MSP is Minimum Support Price and PMI is Purchasing Managers' Index.
SEBI was set up in 1992 and the first ETF in India came in 2002.
SDR value is based on a basket of 5 currencies: Dollar, Euro, Yen, Pound and Yuan.
LEI is a 20-character identifier; D-SIIs named are LIC, GIC and New India Assurance.
DBT began on 1 January 2013; BSBDA is a zero-balance account.
